In celebration of our nation's semiquincentennial, our policy director has created the proposed legislation:

**By Faith American Prosperity and Opportunity Act** 

A BILL 

To promote faith-informed American prosperity and opportunity by providing targeted support to veterans, servicemembers, low-income families, the unemployed, the homeless, the elderly, and all Americans seeking to achieve self-sufficiency and success in the 20th Congressional District of Texas and across the nation, through economic empowerment, workforce development, housing stability, education reform, veterans’ services, and faith-based partnerships.

Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,

SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.

(a) Short Title. This Act may be cited as the “By Faith American Prosperity and Opportunity Act” or the “By Faith PROSPER Act.”

(b) Table of Contents.

SECTION 2. FINDINGS AND PURPOSE.

Congress finds the following:

(1) The United States was founded on principles of faith, liberty, personal responsibility, and opportunity for all Americans, and reliance on God’s providence has historically guided the nation through challenges.

(2) In the 20th Congressional District of Texas (encompassing western San Antonio and parts of Bexar County), persistent poverty, unemployment rates around 4%, housing instability, challenges for veterans and the elderly, and barriers to economic mobility require targeted federal support that prioritizes American citizens and legal residents.

(3) Veterans and servicemembers have sacrificed for the nation and deserve priority access to housing, healthcare, job training, and reintegration services.

(4) Faith-based organizations, churches, and community groups have proven effective in delivering compassionate, results-oriented assistance to the poor, homeless, unemployed, and elderly, often at lower cost and with higher success rates than government programs alone.

(5) Socialism and government overreach have failed to deliver prosperity; instead, policies rooted in free enterprise, education choice, family values, and personal accountability lift individuals and communities.

(b) Purpose. The purpose of this Act is to:

Empower Americans in TX-20 and nationwide through opportunity-focused programs.

Expand support for veterans, soldiers transitioning to civilian life, the poor, the homeless, the unemployed, and the elderly.

Integrate faith-based and community partnerships.
Promote workforce development, housing, education, and economic growth.

Congress will appropriate necessary funds while encouraging private sector and charitable involvement.

SECTION 3. DEFINITIONS.

In this Act:

(1) “American” means a United States citizen or lawful permanent resident.

(2) “Faith-based organization” means a nonprofit organization with a religious mission that provides services without regard to recipients’ faith.

(3) “TX-20” means the 20th Congressional District of Texas.

(4) “Veteran” has the meaning given in section 101 of title 38, United States Code.

(5) “At-risk populations” include the poor, homeless, unemployed, elderly (age 65+), and families in TX-20 facing economic hardship.

TITLE I—ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITY AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT

SEC. 101. TX-20 Prosperity Grants.

(a) The Secretary of Commerce shall establish a grant program providing $250,000,000 annually for 5 years to states for distribution to TX-20 and similar districts for small business incubators, job training in high-demand fields (healthcare, trades, manufacturing, military transition skills), and micro-loans to American entrepreneurs.

(b) Priority to programs partnering with faith-based organizations and veteran-owned businesses.

SEC. 102. Expanded Earned Income Tax Credit and Opportunity Zones.

Enhance the Earned Income Tax Credit for low-income workers in high-poverty areas like parts of TX-20. Designate additional Opportunity Zones in economically distressed neighborhoods of Bexar County.

SEC. 103. Unemployment to Employment Bridge Program.
$100,000,000 for re-skilling and apprenticeships, with bonuses for hiring veterans and long-term unemployed.

TITLE II—VETERANS AND SERVICEMEMBERS SUPPORT

SEC. 201. Veterans Economic Empowerment Initiative.

(a) Authorizes $150,000,000 for expanded VA-Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (HUD-VASH) vouchers, prioritizing TX-20 veterans, including elderly and disabled veterans.

(b) Vocational rehabilitation and employment services tailored to combat medics, drill sergeants, and other military occupational specialties.

SEC. 202. Servicemember Transition Assistance.

Mandatory pre-separation job placement partnerships with private employers and faith-based mentorship programs.

SEC. 203. Major Richard Star Act Alignment.

Coordinates with existing efforts to ensure full benefits for medically retired veterans.

TITLE III—HOUSING AND HOMELESSNESS PREVENTION

SEC. 301. By Faith Housing Stability Fund.

$200,000,000 for grants to faith-based and community organizations providing emergency shelter, transitional housing, rapid re-housing, and permanent supportive housing, with emphasis on veterans and families in TX-20.

SEC. 302. Source of Income Protections.

Encourages states to prohibit discrimination against voucher holders (including veterans) in housing, building on local efforts in San Antonio.

SEC. 303. Elderly Housing Upgrades.

Grants for senior housing modifications, accessibility, and community centers.

TITLE IV—EDUCATION AND CHILD PROTECTION

SEC. 401. School Choice and Workforce Readiness.

Expands education savings accounts and charter school funding for TX-20 families. Prioritizes vocational training and parental rights.

SEC. 402. Child Protection Integration.

Aligns with related legislation protecting children from harmful ideologies while supporting family stability programs.

TITLE V—FAITH-BASED AND COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS

SEC. 501. Charitable Choice Expansion.

Removes barriers to faith-based organizations receiving federal grants for social services, with strong conscience protections.
SEC. 502. By Faith Innovation Grants.

$50,000,000 for pilot programs where churches and nonprofits deliver job placement, addiction recovery, financial literacy, and elder care in TX-20.

TITLE VI—ELDERLY AND GENERAL WELFARE

SEC. 601. Senior Prosperity Program.

Enhanced Medicare/Medicaid flexibility, nutrition programs, and community senior centers with volunteer components.

SEC. 602. Anti-Poverty Innovation.

Block grants encouraging any sexual requirements, marriage destabilization, and one-parent perpetual family support, where evidence-based supports fraud or the perpetration of it. 

SECTION 7. FUNDING AND OVERSIGHT.

(a) Authorization of Appropriations. $1,000,000,000 for fiscal years 2027–2031, with annual reporting to Congress on outcomes in TX-20 (jobs created, housing units provided, veterans served, poverty reduction metrics).

(b) Oversight. Government Accountability Office audit required; preference for programs demonstrating measurable success and minimal administrative overhead.

(c) Sunset. Provisions expire after 5 years unless reauthorized, encouraging efficiency.

SECTION 8. EFFECTIVE DATE.

This Act takes effect 180 days after enactment.
